title: viewer_message is 264 lines and forwards keys three ways
body:
`State::viewer_message` in `compositor.rs` is a 264-line match. The `Hello` arm (about 38 lines) is the welcome handshake and the `Keys` arm (about 40) syncs lock state and pressed keys from the host; both are functions inlined into the dispatch. `keyboard.input::<(), _>(.., Keycode::new(k + 8), state, SERIAL_COUNTER.next_serial(), time, |_, _, _| FilterResult::Forward)` is written at three sites, and the held-key bookkeeping `list.retain(..); if pressed { list.push(..) }` at three. The compositor's `Scroll` struct has the same seven fields as `ViewerMessage::Scroll`, and the arm destructures the variant to rebuild the struct. `out_of_range` is a second full match over `ViewerMessage` that checks sizes, keycodes and selection numbers after decoding. `Key::Swallow` exists because the keyboard filter must return a `Key`; `run_key` matches it to nothing and `repeats` lists it.

## Proposal

- `welcome(id, ..)` and `sync_keys(id, locked, keycodes)` extracted.
- `forward_key(&mut self, evdev, KeyState, time)` and a `hold(list, code, pressed)` helper.
- `ViewerMessage::Scroll(wire::Scroll)` passed straight to `pointer_scroll`.
- `keyboard.input::<Option<Key>, _>` with `menu_key` returning `Option<Key>`, so `Swallow` goes.
- The selection check moves into decoding; see "Selection numbers decode once into an enum at the wire boundary".
close_reason: Landed in 3e2fe5c. viewer_message is 126 lines of dispatch, with welcome, sync_keys, viewer_request and listing extracted. forward_key and hold replace the repeated key code, wire::Scroll goes straight to pointer_scroll, and Key::Swallow is gone. out_of_range stays as it was; the selection check had already moved into decoding.
